Lasso feature selection with cross-validation

Source: R/fs_lasso.R
fs_lasso.Rd

Fits a lasso (or elastic-net) regression with glmnet::cv.glmnet() and selects the predictors whose coefficient is non-zero at the cross-validated penalty. The outcome must be numeric; only the gaussian family is fitted.

Usage

fs_lasso(
  data,
  target,
  alpha = 1,
  nfolds = 5,
  standardize = TRUE,
  custom_folds = NULL,
  impute = c("none", "mean"),
  return_model = FALSE,
  lambda = c("min", "1se"),
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  parallel = FALSE,
  n_cores = 2L
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or data.table holding the target and the candidate predictors, with unique, non-empty column names. A numeric matrix with column names is also accepted. A non-numeric matrix is not: supply a data.frame so factors and characters can be expanded by model.matrix().

target

Single string naming the outcome column in data. It must be numeric and free of NA, NaN and Inf.

alpha

Numeric in (0, 1]; default 1 (lasso). Values in (0, 1) give an elastic net. alpha = 0 (pure ridge) is rejected because ridge never sets a coefficient to exactly zero, so it cannot select.

nfolds

Integer >= 3; default 5. Number of cross-validation folds passed to glmnet::cv.glmnet(), which rejects anything smaller than 3. When custom_folds is supplied, those fold IDs define the folds and nfolds only bounds which IDs are valid, so custom_folds must also define at least 3 folds.

standardize

Logical; default TRUE. Passed to glmnet::cv.glmnet(), and also sets the scale scores is ranked on (see "How scores are scaled").

custom_folds

Optional integer vector of fold IDs, one per row of data, covering 1..nfolds with no empty fold; default NULL.

impute

How to handle missing predictor values: "none" (default) errors and names the affected columns; "mean" imputes column means computed on the full data and warns about the leak.

return_model

Logical; default FALSE. When TRUE, the fitted cv.glmnet object is kept in model and keep = TRUE is passed to cv.glmnet() so the prevalidated fits are retained.

lambda

Penalty to select at: "min" (default, lambda.min) or "1se" (lambda.1se, sparser). See Details.

seed

Optional whole number; default NULL, which leaves the RNG alone. When given, the seed is set for this call only and the previous RNG state is restored on exit.

verbose

Logical; default FALSE. When TRUE, reports the parallel backend status and how many design-matrix columns were selected.

parallel

Logical; default FALSE. When TRUE, cross-validation runs on n_cores workers, which needs the 'doParallel' and 'foreach' packages. If n_cores resolves to one worker, the run stays sequential and says so when verbose = TRUE.

n_cores

Integer >= 1; default 2. Number of workers, used only when parallel = TRUE. Values above the detected core count are capped.

Value

An fs_result object with:

selected

Design-matrix columns whose coefficient at the chosen lambda is non-zero, ordered by decreasing scores magnitude. Constant and numerically constant columns always have coefficient 0, so they are never selected.

scores

data.frame with columns Variable, Coefficient and AbsCoefficient, one row per design-matrix column (including those shrunk to zero), ordered by decreasing AbsCoefficient. On the standardized scale when standardize = TRUE.

method

"lasso", whatever the value of alpha.

task

"regression" (gaussian family only).

model

The fitted cv.glmnet object when return_model = TRUE, else NULL.

details

List of lambda_min (lambda minimizing CV error), lambda_1se (largest lambda within one standard error of the minimum), lambda_used ("lambda.min" or "lambda.1se", the one that selection and all coefficients are read at), coefficients (the same three-column table as scores, always on the raw coefficient scale) and n_features (number of design-matrix columns considered).

call

The matched call.

Details

The lasso adds an L1 penalty to least squares, which shrinks coefficients and sets some of them to exactly zero. fs_lasso() chooses the penalty strength (lambda) by nfolds-fold cross-validation and reports the predictors that keep a non-zero coefficient. With alpha < 1 the penalty becomes an elastic net, a mix of L1 and L2 penalties; fs_elastic() tunes alpha as well and also handles classification.

By default selection happens at lambda.min, the penalty with the lowest cross-validated error. lambda.min is tuned for prediction and tends to over-select, keeping noise variables alongside the true ones. lambda = "1se" selects at lambda.1se, the largest penalty whose CV error is within one standard error of the minimum, which gives a sparser, more conservative set. Both values are reported in details whichever one is used.

The lasso tends to keep one member of a group of strongly correlated predictors and zero out the rest, so an absent feature is not evidence that it is unrelated to the outcome.

fs_lasso() reports no performance estimate. The lambdas are tuned on all rows, so judging the selected set needs an outer resampling loop around the whole call.

How the design matrix is built

Every column of data except target is a candidate predictor. The design matrix comes from stats::model.frame(na.action = stats::na.pass) followed by stats::model.matrix() without an intercept column, so rows with NAs reach the missing-value policy instead of being dropped silently. Factors and characters are expanded to dummy columns: the first factor (in column order) gets one dummy per level and each later factor gets one per level except the first. glmnet fits its own intercept, which is left out of the reported coefficients.

selected, scores and details$coefficients therefore name design-matrix columns, so a factor predictor appears as its dummy columns rather than under its own name. Non-syntactic column names are reported as you wrote them, without the backticks model.matrix() adds.

These inputs are errors:

  • a design matrix with fewer than two columns (glmnet cannot fit a single-column x);

  • a factor or character predictor with fewer than two observed levels;

  • a dummy name that collides with another column or the target (factor g with level b next to a column gb), because selected and scores identify columns by name;

  • Inf or -Inf in any predictor (NaN counts as a missing value);

  • a column whose variance overflows double precision (values around 1e154 or larger); rescale it first.

How scores are scaled

With standardize = TRUE (the default), scores ranks features on the standardized coefficient scale: each coefficient is multiplied by the standard deviation of its design-matrix column, so the ranking does not depend on the units the predictors are measured in. glmnet standardizes internally for fitting but reports coefficients on the input scale, and those raw coefficients are kept in details$coefficients. With standardize = FALSE, scores holds the raw coefficients and the two tables are identical.

A raw coefficient depends on scale: a predictor measured in small units earns a large coefficient for the same effect. Compare details$coefficients (and scores when standardize = FALSE) across predictors only when the predictors share a scale.

Constant columns get a coefficient of exactly 0 and are never selected. The same holds for columns that are constant up to floating-point round-off: standardization would otherwise inflate that round-off into a full-scale predictor with a raw coefficient around 1e15, so such columns are held at 0 during the fit. A coefficient whose standardized value is at most 1e-10 times the largest standardized coefficient is floating-point residue and is set to exactly 0. Without that step, the redundant dummy of the first factor, which is collinear with the intercept, would keep a coefficient around 1e-13 and be selected.

Missing values

Under the default impute = "none", a missing predictor value is an error that names the affected columns, because imputing before cross-validation lets the folds see each other. impute = "mean" fills missing values with column means computed on all rows, not on the training part of each fold, and warns about that leak. A column that is entirely NA is an error under either setting. The target must be free of NA, NaN and Inf.

See also

The Regularization and embedded importance guide, which runs this function on a worked example.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("glmnet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  n <- 100
  df <- data.frame(
    x1 = rnorm(n),
    x2 = rnorm(n),
    cat = sample(letters[1:3], n, TRUE)
  )
  df$y <- 2 * df$x1 - 3 * df$x2 + rnorm(n)
  res <- fs_lasso(df, "y", seed = 123)
  print(selected(res))
  print(head(res$scores))
}
#> [1] "x2"   "x1"   "catc" "cata"
#>   Variable Coefficient AbsCoefficient
#> 1       x2 -2.87232033     2.87232033
#> 2       x1  2.16440132     2.16440132
#> 3     catc -0.09940822     0.09940822
#> 4     cata  0.08988327     0.08988327
#> 5     catb  0.00000000     0.00000000
